name: TPS7A2033PDBVR
title: TPS7A20: 300 mA low-noise, low-IQ, high-PSRR LDO regulator, 1.6 V to 6.0 V input
summary: A single-channel CMOS low-dropout linear regulator for loads up to 300 mA, running from 1.6 V to 6.0 V and built in fixed output voltages from 0.8 V to 5.5 V; the TPS7A2033PDBVR is the 3.3 V version in the 5-pin SOT-23 (DBV) with active output discharge. Its reference is filtered inside the chip, so output noise is about 7 µVRMS (10 Hz to 100 kHz) with no noise capacitor, PSRR reaches 95 dB at 1 kHz, and quiescent current is 6.5 µA typical. It is stable with a 1 µF ceramic output capacitor, holds ±1.5% over line, load and temperature, soft-starts to limit inrush, and has an enable input with an internal pulldown that is released once the pin is driven high. Other versions come in a 1 mm × 1 mm X2SON (DQN) and two 0.6 mm wafer-scale DSBGAs (YCK, YCJ).
key_figures: 3.3 V fixed; family 0.8 V to 5.5 V
145 mV max at 300 mA, 2.5 V ≤ VOUT < 5.5 V, DBV
7 µVRMS typ, 10 Hz to 100 kHz, 300 mA

notes: Ordering code TPS7A20xx(x)Pyyyz: xx(x) is the nominal output voltage, two digits when it falls on a 100 mV step (28 = 2.8 V) and three otherwise (125 = 1.25 V); P marks the active output discharge; yyy is the package (DBV, DQN, YCJ, YCK); z is the packing, R for reel, 3000 pieces for DQN and DBV and 12000 for YCJ and YCK.
Outputs from 0.8 V to 5.5 V can be had in 25 mV steps by asking the factory.
A part marking may carry extra characters for the logo, the lot trace code or the environmental category.
The nominal output voltage and active discharge columns follow the ordering code.

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Supply input. A capacitor of at least the recommended value from IN to GND, mounted tight against the IN and GND pins, lowers the input impedance and helps transient response.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground, common to input and output.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable, active high. Above VEN(HI) the output runs; below VEN(LOW) the regulator shuts off and OUT is pulled to GND. A 500 kΩ internal resistor pulls EN low so the part stays off when the pin floats; it is disconnected while VEN is above VEN(HI), saving input current.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Regulated output. Stability needs a low-ESR capacitor to GND within the recommended range, placed close to OUT and GND. In shutdown (VEN < VEN(LOW)) a 150 Ω typical internal resistor drains the output.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Regulated output; same duty and capacitor needs as on the SOT-23, including the 150 Ω typical shutdown pulldown.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground, common to input and output.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable, active high, with the switched 500 kΩ internal pulldown.

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Supply input; bypass to GND right at the pins.

pins.name: Thermal Pad
pins.function: Exposed pad. Tie it to GND or leave it open, never to any other potential; soldering it to a large ground plane gives the best heat removal.

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Supply input; bypass to GND right at the bumps.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Regulated output; a low-ESR capacitor to GND in the recommended range is needed for stability.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable, active high, with the switched 500 kΩ internal pulldown; pulled low it shuts the output down and drains OUT.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground, common to input and output.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The regulator with only its two capacitors. The supply comes in at INPUT with 1.0 µF from IN to ground, the regulated rail leaves at OUTPUT with 1.0 µF from OUT to ground, and ENABLE switches the output on when driven high. The worked example uses the 2.8 V version (TPS7A2028) from a 3.3 V nominal supply (3.1 V to 3.6 V) at up to 200 mA and 85 °C ambient; some loads need more than 1 µF on either side.

output capacitor, low-ESR ceramic, at least 1 µF

operation.text: A low-noise, high-PSRR, low-IQ LDO aimed at RF and precision analog supplies. It needs no separate noise-filter capacitor and runs with one 1 µF input capacitor and one 1 µF ceramic output capacitor. Inside are a bandgap reference, an error amplifier driving the pass device, a current limit, UVLO, thermal shutdown, an internal controller, the 500 kΩ enable pulldown and, on P versions, an active output discharge.

Noise from the reference passes through an internal first-order RC low-pass with a corner near 0.1 Hz before it reaches the output buffer. While the part starts, the filter resistance is taken out of the path so the output can rise fast; the filter returns to normal once the output has reached its set value.

EN is active high: above VEN(HI) the output turns on, below VEN(LOW) it turns off. With EN floating, the internal pulldown REN(PULLDOWN) holds the part off; once EN is driven above VEN(HI) that resistor is disconnected to save quiescent current. Where the output needs no separate control, EN can be tied to IN.

Dropout is VIN - VOUT at the rated current with the pass transistor fully on, acting as a switch in its ohmic region. It sets the lowest input above the nominal output that keeps regulation; below that, the output follows the input down. Because the pass device is CMOS, dropout is set by its on-resistance and shrinks in proportion at lighter loads.

The limit is a mix of brick-wall and foldback. With the output above VFOLDBACK, current is held at ICL; below VFOLDBACK the allowed current falls as the output approaches ground, reaching ISC into a short. The output is not regulated while limiting, and the pass device dissipates (VIN - VOUT) × ICL or (VIN - VOUT) × ISC. If that trips thermal shutdown the part turns off, restarts when cool, and keeps cycling between limit and shutdown while the fault lasts.

A separate UVLO watches VIN so the output turns on and off cleanly; its hysteresis keeps a dip during turn-on from shutting the part off. Below the rising threshold the device does not start. A brownout that stays above the falling threshold (rising threshold minus hysteresis) can let the output sag but leaves the device on. A dip below the falling threshold disables it in most cases, the output decays through the load and the discharge circuit, and the part starts up again in the usual way once VIN climbs back past the rising threshold.

The LDO switches off when the pass transistor junction reaches TSD (165 °C typical rising) and back on when it cools to the reset point (140 °C typical). The die heats and cools fast, so the part can cycle on and off until dissipation comes down. A large VIN - VOUT at start-up or inrush into a big output capacitor can trip it before start-up completes. Operation is specified only up to TJ = 125 °C; running into shutdown or above that limit for long periods shortens the part's life, and the protection is no substitute for heat sinking.

On P versions a transistor inside switches a resistor between OUT and ground whenever the device is disabled, by EN low or by VIN falling below the UVLO threshold, to drain the output capacitor. It is not meant for emptying a large output capacitance after the input has collapsed: current can then flow backward from output to input and damage the device. Reverse current is to stay below 5% of the rated current, and only briefly.

Normal regulation needs VIN above VOUT(nom) + VDO, load below the current limit, TJ below the shutdown point, and EN having risen past its rising threshold without since falling below its falling threshold. In dropout (VIN below VOUT(nom) + VDO, everything else normal) the output follows the input and line or load steps cause large excursions. Coming out of a steady dropout state, the output can overshoot briefly while the pass device returns to its linear region. Driving EN below VEN(LOW) turns the pass device and internal circuits off and the output is discharged to ground.

Low-ESR multilayer ceramics are the intended input and output capacitors. X7R, X5R and C0G dielectrics hold their value reasonably over temperature; Y5V is discouraged for its large variation. Effective capacitance drops with bias and temperature, by as much as 50%, and the recommended values already allow for about half the nominal value. An input capacitor of at least the nominal value is advised when source impedance exceeds 0.5 Ω, and a larger one for fast, large line or load steps or when the source is more than a few centimetres away. The output capacitor must stay inside the recommended range.

On a step from light to heavy load the output first dips as the output capacitor supplies charge through its parasitic impedance, then recovers as the LDO raises its current. On a step back to light load the output first rises while the LDO is still sourcing heavily, then recovers as the LDO cuts back and the load drains the capacitor. More output capacitance lowers the peaks but slows the response; a larger standing load also lowers the peaks.

Keep other heat sources away from the regulator on the board. Dissipation is roughly (VIN - VOUT) × IOUT, so choosing rails with the least headroom gives the best efficiency. Heat leaves mainly through the thermal pad, which is soldered to a copper area with an array of plated vias to inner or bottom planes. RθJA in the thermal table comes from a JEDEC standard board and only ranks packages; on a real board it is the X2SON junction-to-case (bottom) resistance plus whatever the copper adds. The ψJT and ψJB metrics depend little on copper area and estimate TJ from a measured top or board temperature.

Output current against VIN - VOUT is bounded by dropout at small headroom, by the 300 mA rating in the middle, and by junction temperature at large headroom, where allowed current falls along IOUT = (TJ - TA) / [RθJA × (VIN - VOUT)]; the input voltage range sets the lowest and highest VIN - VOUT. The boundary is drawn for a JEDEC high-K board with the RθJA of the thermal table.

Run from a well-regulated, quiet supply of 1.6 V to 6.0 V. For full regulation and dynamic performance VIN should not drop below VOUT(nom) + 0.3 V or 1.6 V, whichever is higher. A 1 µF or larger input capacitor is strongly advised to lower source impedance during transients.

Mount both capacitors right beside the regulator, give its pins wide copper planes to carry heat away, and spread heat with thermal vias around the part. Do not put a thermal via directly under the DQN thermal pad: it can draw solder away from the pad joint during reflow. CIN connects IN to the ground copper and COUT connects OUT to the ground copper on the component side, with EN brought out on its own trace.

For a 2.8 V rail at up to 200 mA from a 3.3 V nominal supply, the TPS7A2028 is used with at least 1.0 µF at the input, to counter the resistance and inductance between source and LDO, and at least 1.0 µF at the output for stability and load-step response. Dropout is under 140 mV at 2.8 V and 300 mA, so a supply as low as 3.0 V leaves enough headroom at 200 mA.
